'''Robert E Fontana''' is an engineer, physicist, and author who is noted for his contributions in the areas of [[magnetic recording]] and [[data storage]] on [[hard disk drives]] (HDD) and on digital [[tape recorders]].<ref name="bio">[https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37304917500 IEEE Xplore author profile: Robert E. Fontana]</ref>  His work has concentrated on developing thin film processing techniques for nano-fabrication of magnetic devices including [[Giant Magnetoresistance]] read heads now used universally in magnetic recording. Much of his career was with [[IBM]] in San Jose, California. He is a [[Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] and a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]].

== Background and education ==
Fontana grew up in [[Champaign, Illinois]].<ref name="Spectrum" /> He received a Bachelor's, a Master's, and a Ph.D. degrees all from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) Department of [[Electrical Engineering]] in 1969, 1971, and 1975, respectively.<ref name="dist" />  Fontana completed his Ph.D. on the optical and magnetic properties of thin films under the direction of Professor David J. Epstein.

== Career ==
Fontana joined [[Texas instruments]] in [[Dallas, Texas]], in 1975 to work on magnetic [[bubble memory]] devices. He had been originally introduced to magnetic bubble memory in 1970 in an IEEE lecture by Andrew Eschenfelder<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oralhistory.rutgers.edu/alphabetical-index/interviewees/30-interview-html-text/1551-eschenfelder-andrew|title=Eschenfelder, Andrew|first=Shaun R.|last=Illingworth|website=oralhistory.rutgers.edu}}</ref> of IBM.<ref name="accept" /> He was encouraged in this work by Dennis Bus<ref>{{Cite journal|title=In Memory of Dennis D. Buss [In Memoriam]|first=Jesus A.|last=del Alamo|date=May 17, 2019|journal=IEEE Solid-State Circuits Magazine|volume=11|issue=2|pages=139|doi=10.1109/MSSC.2019.2909223|s2cid=197435235 |doi-access=free}}</ref> who was also a visiting scientist at MIT and by Dean Toombs, the VP in charge of bubbles at TI<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/08/04/archives/ti-sets-bubble-memory-texas-instruments-set-to-sell-bubble-memories.html|title=T.I.Sets Bubble Memory|first=Peter J.|last=Schuyten|work=The New York Times |date=August 4, 1978|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref>

In 1981, Fontana joined the [https://research.ibm.com/labs/almaden/ IBM Almaden Research Center] in San Jose, California, to work on thin film [[Disk read-and-write head|magnetic recording heads]]. He made significant contributions in the development of processing of both inductive write heads and three generations of magnetoresistive read heads.<ref>{{Cite interview |last=Dieny |first=Bernard |subject-link=Bernard Dieny |interviewer=[[Christopher H. Bajorek|Chris Bajorek]] |title=Invention, Development and Commercialization of GMR Heads oral history panel |last2=Gurney |first2=Bruce |subject-link2=Bruce Gurney|last3=Pinarbasi |first3=Mustafa |last4=Speriosu |first4=Virgil |url=https://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/access/text/2019/09/102781311-05-01-acc.pdf |publisher=[[Computer History Museum]] |date=May 30, 2019 |page=29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/access/text/2016/01/102737911-05-01-acc.pdf|title=Computer History Museum: Oral History of Frederick (Rick) H. Dill, Interviewed by: David Laws, Recorded: June 11, 2015}}</ref> These included Anisotropic [[Magnetoresistance]] (AMR) heads, [[Giant Magnetoresistance]] (GMR) heads. and [[Tunnel magnetoresistance]] (TMR) heads.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Childress |first1=Jeffrey R. |last2=Fontana |first2=Robert E. |date=2005 |title=Magnetic recording read head sensor technology |url=https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/physique/articles/10.1016/j.crhy.2005.11.001/ |journal=Comptes Rendus. Physique |language=en |volume=6 |issue=9 |pages=997–1012 |doi=10.1016/j.crhy.2005.11.001 |bibcode=2005CRPhy...6..997C |issn=1878-1535|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Fontana's colleagues and collaborators included Ta Lin Hsu, Ching Tsang, [[Christopher Bajorek]], [https://ethw.org/Heiner_Sussner Heiner Sussner], Prakash Kasiraj, Bob Scranton, [https://ethw.org/Frederick_H._Dill Rick Dill].<ref name="accept" />

From 2003 to 2007, Fontana worked for [[Hitachi GST]] (a result of [[Hitachi]]'s purchase of IBM's disk-drive division). His work at Hitachi GST at that time focussed on nano structure e-beam fabrication and on novel flux detecting sensors including all-metal CPP GMR sensors that scale well to very small device sizes.<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{Cite journal|title=All-Metal Current-Perpendicular-to-Plane Giant Magnetoresistance Sensors for Narrow-Track Magnetic Recording|first1=J. R.|last1=Childress|first2=M. J.|last2=Carey|first3=S.|last3=Maat|first4=N.|last4=Smith|first5=R. E.|last5=Fontana|first6=D.|last6=Druist|first7=K.|last7=Carey|first8=J. A.|last8=Katine|first9=N.|last9=Robertson|first10=T. D.|last10=Boone|first11=M.|last11=Alex|first12=J.|last12=Moore|first13=C. H.|last13=Tsang|date=January 17, 2008|journal=IEEE Transactions on Magnetics|volume=44|issue=1|pages=90–94|doi=10.1109/TMAG.2007.911019|bibcode=2008ITM....44...90C |s2cid=29454559 }}</ref>

In 2008, Fontana re-joined the IBM Almaden Research Center to work on heads for magnetic tape recording.<ref name="bio" /> In particular he contributed to the development and implementation of TMR read heads suitable for the harsh tape recording environment.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fontana |first1=R. E. |last2=Biskeborn |first2=R. G. |last3=Lantz |first3=M. |last4=Decad |first4=G. M. |date=2019 |title=Tape in the cloud—Technology developments and roadmaps supporting 80 TB cartridge capacities |journal=AIP Advances |language=en |volume=9 |issue=12 |article-number=125222 |doi=10.1063/1.5130404 |bibcode=2019AIPA....9l5222F |issn=2158-3226|doi-access=free }}</ref> In addition, Fontana published several papers with S. Hetzler and G. Decad examining the global market and technology outlook for data storage technologies in general comparing solid-state, optical, hard disk drive, and tape.<ref name="future">{{Cite journal |last1=Fontana |first1=R. E. |last2=Decad |first2=G. M. |last3=Hetzler |first3=S. R. |date=2015 |title=Volumetric density trends (TB/in.3) for storage components: TAPE, hard disk drives, NAND, and Blu-ray |url=https://pubs.aip.org/jap/article/117/17/17E301/391692/Volumetric-density-trends-TB-in-3-for-storage |journal=Journal of Applied Physics |language=en |volume=117 |issue=17 |article-number=17E301 |doi=10.1063/1.4906208 |issn=0021-8979|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

During his career, Fontana played an important role in several technical societies including the [[National Academy of Engineering]] and the [[National Research Council (United States)|National Research Council]]. In particular, he played an influential role with the [https://www.ieeemagnetics.org/ IEEE Magnetics Society] encouraged by [[Charles Denis Mee|Denis Mee]], [[Mark Kryder]], and [[:de:David Thompson (Ingenieur)|Dave Thompson]]. Fontana served on the 'MagSoc' Administrative Committee and in various roles supporting IEEE conferences. For example, Fontana was Conference Chair for the joint MMM/Intermag conference in 2004.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Chairman's Preface|first=R.E.|last=Fontana|date=July 17, 2004|journal=IEEE Transactions on Magnetics|volume=40|issue=4|pages=1991|doi=10.1109/TMAG.2004.832661|bibcode=2004ITM....40.1991F }}</ref>  In 2001 and 2002, he served as president of the IEEE Magnetics Society<ref name="president">{{Cite web|url=https://ieeemagnetics.org/index.php_option=com_content&view=article&id=254&Itemid=173|title=IEEE Magnetics Society Presidents, 1965-2019}}</ref> and was formally recognized for his long-standing contributions to the Society in 2017.<ref name="service" />

Fontana was a Consulting Professor at [[Stanford University]] Materials Science and Engineering from 2006 to 2011<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.stanford.edu/dept/registrar/bulletin1112/5303.htm|title=Stanford Bulletin - Stanford University|first=Office of the Registrar-Stanford|last=University|website=web.stanford.edu}}</ref>

Fontana retired from IBM in July 2021.  He lives in [[San Jose, California]].{{cn|date=April 2022}}

== Awards and recognition ==
Fontana has been recognized internationally and received multiple awards for his contributions to magnetic recording technology and his leadership in the engineering community:
*Fellow [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]], 1996<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ieeemagnetics.org/ieee_static_content/Newsletters/Newsletter/July96/index.html|title=IEEE Magnetics Society Newsletter July 1996|website=ieeemagnetics.org}}</ref> "for development of novel processes for magnetic devices, most notably magneto-resistive thin film heads" 
*[[IEEE Cledo Brunetti Award]], 2000. This is a technical field award from IEEE for "outstanding contributions to nanotechnology and technologies for microsystem miniaturization".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieee.org/content/dam/ieee-org/ieee/web/org/about/awards/recipients/brunetti-rl.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216193824/https://www.ieee.org/content/dam/ieee-org/ieee/web/org/about/awards/recipients/brunetti-rl.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 16, 2021|title=IEEE Cledo Brunetti Award recipients|website=[[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) }}</ref><ref name = "Spectrum">{{Cite journal|title=The IEEE Technical Field Awards [Awards]|date=August 17, 2000|journal=IEEE Spectrum|volume=37|issue=8|pages=58–70|doi=10.1109/MSPEC.2000.8736474}}</ref> Fontana's citation reads: "for contributions to micro fabrication techniques for the manufacture of thin film and giant magnetoresistive heads used in hard disk drives" 
*Member [[National Academy of Engineering]] 2002<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nae.edu/30624/Dr-Robert-E-Fontana-Jr|title=Dr. Robert E. Fontana, Jr.|website=NAE Website}}</ref> "For contributions to microfabrication techniques for the manufacture of thin-film storage devices" 
*IEEE Magnetics Society Distinguished Lecturer, 2005<ref name="dist">[https://ieeemagnetics.org/ieee_static_content/Newsletters/Newsletter/05october/Oct2005_Newsletter.pdf "Distinguished Lecturers For 2005", IEEE Magnetics Society Newsletter, Volume 44, No. 4, p. 9, October 2005]</ref> "Micro-Fabrication Techniques for Magnetic Information Storage Devices: From Bubbles to Thin-Film Recording Heads to Nanomagnetic Structures" 
*IEEE Magnetics Society Achievement Award, 2005, the highest award offered by the Magnetics Society<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ieeemagnetics.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=90:2005-achievement-award&catid=66&Itemid=97|title=2005 Achievement Award|website=ieeemagnetics.org}}</ref><ref name="accept">[https://ieeemagnetics.org/ieee_static_content/Newsletters/Newsletter/05october/Oct2005_Newsletter.pdf "Magnetics Society Achievement Award: acceptance speech", IEEE Magnetics Society Newsletter, Volume 44, No. 4, p. 16, October 2005]</ref> 
*IEEE Magnetics Society Distinguished Service Award, 2017<ref name="service">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieeemagnetics.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=256&Itemid=176|title=Previous recipients of the Distinguished Service Award|website=www.ieeemagnetics.org}}</ref> "for establishing the structure and enhancing the international impact of major technical conferences sponsored by the IEEE Magnetics Society"

== Patents and publications ==
Fontana is the author or coauthor of 141 US. patents<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/robert-e-fontana?|title=Robert E. Fontana Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref> as well as 61 publications in scientific and engineering journals.<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Robert-E-Fontana-2095404257|title=Researchgate: publications: Robert E. Fontana}}</ref> The majority of these are in the area of thin film processing applied to nanometer-scale magnetic transducers for magnetic data storage in hard disk drives and digital tape recorders. Several more recent publications address the status and outlook comparing solid-state, optical, HDD and tape storage technologies<ref name="future" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://storageconference.us/2018/Presentations/Fontana.pdf|title=R. Fontana, G. Decad, "R. Fontana, G. Decad, "A Ten Year (2008-2017) Storage Landscape: LTO Tape Media, HDD, NAND" MSST 2018, Santa Clara, May 14-16, 2018|access-date=2022-03-10|archive-date=2020-03-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200310054601/https://storageconference.us/2018/Presentations/Fontana.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
